title: Case intake agent live at L1 in rwb-agent: the service login, the decision code, the business date of the stale check, the acceptance event name, the list codes, the case-decision proposal path, the route path, the feature flag home, the topic and migration values and the policy values the gate reads are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-028 sections 3, 4, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.7 and A2.6.3.1; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P10-010 and API-P10-011; context pack P10 (service row, the eight tables, the eleven REST operations, EV-28, AgentRunWorkflow and the naming rules); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.4, R5.5 DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-13, DP-15 and DP-19, and R9; Ownership Map v1 as repeated in the context pack (tables agent_run, agent_policy, agent_prompt and agent_feedback under P10; api rows GET /cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs and POST /agent-runs/{runId}/feedback under P10)
section: 3. Preconditions; 5. Exception paths; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC9; 8. Business rules BR1 to BR3; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.1 to 12.3; 13. Solution plan; 15. Screens and states
description: The app slice needs values that no source fixes, and none of them is invented. (1) The per-service login of rwb-agent is required by DP-02, and the legacy section 10 names only the agent identity SY-AGENT and the roles. (2) The decision code D6 is the assumed code of LOV-DECISION in the legacy BR3. (3) The business date against which agent_run.data_as_of is compared for the stale warning of AC9 has no owner operation in this key, because the freshness rule of the FSD names v_ace_batch_status, which belongs to rwb-source-data and is not a dependency of this service. (4) The catalogue of the agent topic names only AgentRunCompleted, so the name of the acceptance event is a settled value. (5) The seven list codes are named in the legacy story but no source says which service holds their values, and DP-07 makes them rwb-case's. (6) The path of the case-decision proposal operation of rwb-case is not published. (7) The path and the name of the gateway-bff route in front of the two operations are not specified, although DP-19 requires the route. (8) The legacy feature flag rwb.agent.intake-l1 has no home once the monolith property file is gone. (9) The partition count, replication factor and retention of the two topics and the names of their retry and .dlt topics are not fixed. (10) The place of V10_008__agent_feedback.sql in the service's Flyway ordering is not fixed, because no source lists the P10 migration sequence. (11) The item key set of an intake output is not listed; the legacy story fixes the item SUMMARY only, and the status and the message of a verdict outside LOV-FEEDBACK are not stated. (12) The mode, the segment, the segment threshold, the confidence floor and the timeout the gate reads are rows of an approved policy version whose load path belongs to RWB-P10-E1061-CON, and no source says so in the words of this key. The story keeps every legacy value - the policy version P2, the mode L1, the prompt PR3, the decision code D6, the item SUMMARY, the 1,000 characters of the reason and the nine acceptance criteria - and settles each open value as an assumption row of this WP.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 3 (the approved policy P2 with mode L1 from 2027-01-25), section 4 (the orchestrator run and the decision log write), section 7 AC1 to AC9, section 8 BR1 (only runs in mode L1 for the case segment are returned), BR3 (decision D6, LOV-DECISION, assumed code) and BR5 (one feedback per run and item; the intake summary is item SUMMARY), section 10 (roles only, no login name), section 11 (DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-060 and DF-AGT-097 to DF-AGT-102) and section 12 (the two operations on the monolith base, AgentOutput, AgentFeedbackRequest, the decision log mapping and the errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503), section 13 (migration V10_008__agent_feedback.sql, the components and the feature flag rwb.agent.intake-l1); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.7.3.1 VR-P10-007-1 (v_ace_batch_status, MSG-P1-001) and A2.6.3.1 VR-P10-006-1 (MSG-GEN-001); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.0 (standard columns), T3.1 (DF-AGT-008 to DF-AGT-011, DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-060, DF-AGT-097 to DF-AGT-102), T3.2 (LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-FEEDBACK, LOV-DECISION, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-REGION) and T-A.2 API-P10-010 and API-P10-011; context pack P10 (schema rwb_agent, base /api/recovery/agent/v1, topic rwb.agent.events.v1, queue rwb-agent, EV-28, AgentRunWorkflow and the naming and shared platform rules); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.4, R5.5 and R9
area: Agent runtime: identity, decision record, stale check, event name, lists, proposal path, route, feature flag, topic and migration values, policy values
owner_role: Solution architect with the P10 service owner and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-source-data
proposed: Name the service identity 'the rwb-agent login (DP-02)' with grants on rwb_agent only. Read the decision code D6 as the LOV-DECISION value of the approved policy row and write the record through the local library. Compare agent_run.data_as_of with the business date of the rwb-source-data freshness read. Name the acceptance event rwb.agent.AgentFeedbackRecorded.v1 under R4. Read the seven lists through the rwb-case reference-data contract with their codes as service configuration. Build the case-decision proposal against the fake of RWB-P3-E1035-CON until its path is published. Reach the two operations through one gateway-bff pass-through route of one hop. Hold rwb.agent.intake-l1 as a data row of the platform feature-flag library. Provision both topics with a retry and a .dlt topic and leave partitions, replication and retention as environment values. Keep the legacy file name V10_008__agent_feedback.sql and let the sequence order decide its place. Keep SUMMARY as the only item and refuse another verdict with 422 and MSG-GEN-001. Read the mode, the segment, the segment threshold, the confidence floor and the timeout from the approved policy row. Every default is carried by an assumption row and is confirmed at the wave 2 contract freeze with the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-source-data and the platform libraries.

title: Case intake agent at L1 contract in rwb-agent: the member types of the answer and of the request, the acceptance event name, the case-decision proposal path, the route path, the 409 rule, the item key set, the invalid-verdict refusal and the policy values are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-028 sections 7, 11 and 12; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6.3.1; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P10-010 and API-P10-011; context pack P10 (base, topic, queue, EV-28, ownership rows and naming rules); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.4, R5.5 DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-13, DP-15 and DP-19, and R9; Ownership Map v1 as repeated in the context pack
section: 3. Preconditions; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC8; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.1 to 12.3; 15. Screens and states
description: The contract slice needs eight values that no source fixes. (1) The legacy story names the members of AgentOutput and of AgentFeedbackRequest and the TSD gives the table columns and three lengths, but no source gives the REST member types, the maximum length of summary and gapType beyond the table, or the form of the feedback member inside the answer. (2) DP-03 names the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 and not the event type, and the catalogue names only AgentRunCompleted on the agent topic, so the acceptance event name is a settled value. (3) The path of the case-decision proposal operation of rwb-case is not published. (4) The path and the name of the gateway-bff route in front of the two operations are not specified, although DP-19 requires the route. (5) The legacy operation carries both the If-Match header and the one-feedback-per-run-and-item rule and gives one message for both, and no source states which check answers the 409 first. (6) The item key set is not listed, and the legacy story fixes SUMMARY only. (7) The status and the message of a verdict outside LOV-FEEDBACK are not stated. (8) The member names of the eligibility answer beyond those this document names, and the policy values it reads, are not fixed by a source. The contract keeps the legacy members and values, settles each open value as an assumption row, and declares no monolith path and no table of another service.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 7 (the nine criteria and their values), section 11 (DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-060 and DF-AGT-097 to DF-AGT-102) and section 12 (GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs, POST /api/recovery/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback, AgentOutput with runId, agent, agentVersion, mode, status, summary, gaps, confidence, dataAsOf and feedback, AgentFeedbackRequest with itemKey, verdict and reason at most 1,000 characters, the If-Match header, the errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 and the one-feedback-per-run-and-item rule); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (agent_feedback: item_key varchar(20), verdict varchar(10), reason varchar(1000)), T3.2 (LOV-FEEDBACK, LOV-AUTONOMY) and T-A.2 API-P10-010 and API-P10-011; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6.3.1 VR-P10-006-1 (MSG-GEN-001); context pack P10 (base /api/recovery/agent/v1, topic rwb.agent.events.v1, queue rwb-agent, EV-28 and the ownership rows under P10); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.4, R5.5 and R9
area: Contract: answer and request member types, acceptance event name, proposal path, route path, conflict rule, item key set, invalid-verdict refusal, eligibility answer
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the solution architect and the owners of rwb-case and rwb-decision
proposed: Fix the two operations on the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 with the legacy members and the legacy refusals; fix the member names of the answer and of the request and leave the physical types and lengths to the review with their owners. Declare the acceptance event as rwb.agent.AgentFeedbackRecorded.v1 and the record as DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1, both with the retry and .dlt topics. Build the case-decision proposal against the fake of RWB-P3-E1035-CON. Publish the two operations behind one gateway-bff pass-through route of one hop and 2 s and take its path from the edge contract. Settle the 409 by the unique key of agent_run_id and item_key first and the If-Match version second, both carrying MSG-GEN-004. Keep SUMMARY as the only item key and refuse a verdict outside LOV-FEEDBACK with 422 and MSG-GEN-001. Read the eligibility members from the approved policy row. Each open value is carried by an assumption row and is confirmed at the contract freeze with the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision and the edge.

title: Case intake agent at L1 deployment in rwb-agent: the login, the route path, the topic partitions, retry and retention, the migration order, the alert window and thresholds, the worker and probe values and the consumer groups are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-028 sections 3, 4, 5 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.7; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T7; context pack P10 (schema rwb_agent, topic rwb.agent.events.v1, queue rwb-agent, namespace rwb-recovery, EV-28 and the naming and shared platform rules); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.5 DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19, and R9; Ownership Map v1 as repeated in the context pack
section: 3. Preconditions; 5. Exception paths; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC9; 8. Business rules BR1 to BR12; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.1 to 12.7; 13. Solution plan
description: The deployment story needs values that no source carries, and it must not invent one: the login name of the rwb-agent service; the path and the name of the gateway-bff route in front of the two operations; the partition count, replication factor and retention of rwb.agent.events.v1 and of the shared rwb.decision-record.v1, and the names of their retry and .dlt topics; the relay interval of the outbox; the place of V10_008__agent_feedback.sql in the service's Flyway ordering; the window after which an alert fires and the floors and ceilings of the acceptance and override series, the worker build ID, the version set, the worker minimum and maximum, the activity timeouts, the probe paths and timings, the replica counts, the resource sizes, the host, the SKU and the budget; the dashboard series retention; and the consumer groups of the agent topic, which belong to the services that consume it. The legacy story fixes the migration file name, the table agent_feedback, the feature flag rwb.agent.intake-l1 and the messages MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P7-005 and MSG-GEN-004, and those values are kept as they are; every other number is a value of the environment, not of this story. Each missing value is carried by the placeholder of R9 and one assumption row.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 3 (the approved policy and the case owner rights), section 4 (the run, the panel read and the feedback write), section 5 (X3, the incident and R-UNI-39) and section 13 (migration V10_008__agent_feedback.sql, the components and the feature flag rwb.agent.intake-l1); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T7 (NFR-008, NFR-009, NFR-010); context pack P10 (one schema and one login per service, the topic with its retry and .dlt topics, the task queue rwb-agent in namespace rwb-recovery, the gateway-bff route and the no-PII rule); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.5 and R9
area: Operations: identity, route path, topic values and rights, migration order, alert window and thresholds, worker and probe values, retirement of the dashboard series and consumer groups
owner_role: Platform administrator with the DevOps team and the ACE database team
proposed: Reference the login through a secret and never a literal; run the migration job as a pre-deploy job of the per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_agent with the legacy file name and a forward-only rollback; provision both topics from the platform topic module with their retry and .dlt topics and the publish right of rwb-agent, and verify the consume rights of rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-deviation and rwb-reporting without creating their groups in rwb-agent; deploy the worker with the release build ID on the version set and KEDA on backlog; wire the reference lists and the freshness read through their contracts and hold rwb.agent.intake-l1 as a platform flag row, off in DEV and on in SIT and UAT after the smoke read; publish the two operations behind the gateway-bff pass-through route; wire six alerts and six runbook entries and rehearse the rollback in SIT. Each value is carried by an assumption row and is fixed per environment at the release review.
